Question B-002-008-008.

Why the correct answer is right: For a portable high-frequency (HF) emergency setup, a dipole or vertical is practical because it can be carried and put up fairly simply.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "A parabolic dish": At HF wavelengths, a useful dish would be very large, so it is not a general portable HF emergency antenna.
- sourceIndex 2: "A three-element Yagi": A three-element Yagi is larger and more complex than the simple portable HF options expected for quick emergency setup.
- sourceIndex 3: "A three-element quad": A three-element quad also needs bulky support structure, which works against a portable HF station that must be set up quickly.
